correct_completion: she would have caught the train.
full_sentence: Had she left earlier, she would have caught the train.
acceptable_variants: she would have made it onto the train.
she could have caught the train.

options.text: she is a very punctual person.
options.why_wrong: This describes a general trait and does not complete the inverted third conditional set up by 'had'.

options.text: she will catch the train tomorrow.
options.why_wrong: An inverted 'had' clause refers to an unreal past situation, so a future result does not fit.

options.text: the train was delayed last night.
options.why_wrong: This gives a past fact but not the main clause result that an inverted conditional requires.

options.text: she would have caught the train.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional with 'had' instead of 'if'
explanation: In an inverted third conditional, 'had' starts the clause instead of 'if', and the main clause uses would have plus a past participle. Learners sometimes choose a future form, which breaks the link to the unreal past.
translation: Якби вона пішла раніше, вона б встигла на потяг.
